about: Names that look right and are wrong on this engine: each one cost a feature that silently never ran. Suite `known-false` checks every verified-on-engine entry against the member tables recorded from the real engine (truth/engine-members.json) or against a recorded answer (truth/engine-facts.txt), so the list cannot rot: if an engine update makes a name real, the suite fails and the entry is removed. `is`: absent (not a member), function (it exists but as a method, so a bare read is a function and always truthy), property (it exists but calling it throws), no-overload (the method exists, but not with `args` arguments), no-signature (the method exists, but not with these argument types), fact (the recorded answer to `fact` is `answer`). `real` lists replacement names that must exist on the same class. read-only entries were established by reading or by an earlier session and are NOT re-checked here. A future lint rule can read this file.

entries.instead: inv.slots (KubeJS) or inv.containerSize: 41 = main 0-35, armor 36-39, off hand 40; `inv.size` is undefined, so `for (i < inv.size)` runs zero times
inv.getSlots() / inv.getContainerSize()
inv.getStackInSlot(i)
String(x) (or '' + x) before a Set / Map lookup, or a plain object as the table: stack.id, entity.type, block.id are wrapped Java strings
String(x) first
String(x).length: on the raw value `length` is Java's length() METHOD, so `x.length > 0` is false
String(x).replace(...): on the raw value it is Java's replace(CharSequence, CharSequence), which takes the regex as literal text and changes nothing
stack.enchantments is a map of id -> level; or EnchantmentHelper.getItemEnchantmentLevel(ench, stack)
stack.nbt (KubeJS renames getTag to getNbt)
stack.nbt = tag
stack.hasNBT(): hasTag(id) is KubeJS's item-TAG test and takes one argument, so `stack.hasTag` is truthy and `stack.hasTag()` throws
nothing: an ItemStack in a script is already the raw stack
Item.of(id) is the stack
stack.isEmpty() with parens (or stack.empty): the bare name is a function reference, always truthy
entity.attack(source, amount) (KubeJS renames hurt)
entity.age: `tickCount` reads undefined
entity.level (a property): the vanilla level() method is hidden, so entity.level() throws
entity.uuid / entity.getUuid()
entity.setMotion(x, y, z): setDeltaMovement only takes a Vec3
entity.getItemBySlot(slot) or the KubeJS getters (mainHandItem, headArmorItem, ...)

entity.getX() / entity.x, or call the method pos.x(): Vec3 has a field AND a method named x, and a value read of pos.x throws a NullPointerException that no script catch catches and that ends the event for every later handler (same for y, z)
level.time (KubeJS renames getGameTime to getTime): `level.gameTime` is undefined and a clock built on it is NaN
level.getTime()
level.dayTime() with parens: the bare name is a function, not a number
level.isClientSide() with parens: the bare name is always truthy
entity.spawnAtLocation(stack), or player.give(stack)
source.actual (KubeJS renames getEntity to getActual)
source.getActual()
source.immediate
source.getImmediate()
source.getType() for the message id, source.type().msgId(), or source.is(tag): `source.type` is the vanilla type() METHOD, so String(source.type) never equals an id
source.getType()
nothing: no class in the pack has it; the only crit a script can see is the pack's own roll
event.damage (EntityEvents.hurt)
victim.getLastHurtByMob(): the knockback event has no source
append(Text.of('...')) or pass the string and let the Component wrapper convert it: append(String) is hidden

it returns the DEFAULT key (minecraft:pig, minecraft:air) without an error: pass the registry object (entity.getEntityType()), never the id string
pass a BlockPos or [x, y, z]: an object literal becomes BlockPos.ZERO
cancel() throws to leave the handler: make it the last statement, outside any try (lint rules AFTER-EXIT, CANCEL-IN-TRY)
